Project-C is a strategic independent commercial project under the SSCCS
initiative, currently in its early architecture phase.

Every data system today pays a hidden structural cost that has been treated
as inevitable. The industry has spent decades optimizing around it — faster
hardware, smarter caching, bigger indexes — without addressing the mechanism
itself. Project-C was built from the observation that this cost is not
structural at all; it is a property of how data is addressed, not how it is
stored. Change the addressing model, and the entire cost profile changes with
it.

While the infrastructure market pours resources into faster databases and
more sophisticated storage engines, the fundamental bottleneck remains
untouched. Project-C targets this bottleneck directly, making it irrelevant
rather than optimizing around it. The result is a layer that fits beneath
existing infrastructure and accelerates everything above it, without
requiring migration or architectural changes.

The addressing model scales cleanly from embedded sensors to datacenter
production caches, from LLM inference pipelines to real-time robotics
fusion. It works in environments where traditional index structures cannot
survive — radiation-rich space, latency-critical edge deployments,
consumer devices with no cloud dependency. The same arithmetic that resolves
a lookup in nanoseconds today provides the foundation for hardware
integration at the memory controller and pipeline level when the application
demands it.
